record.detail: The UK sanctioned Legend Innovation, described as operator of '#8 Park' (reported capacity for 20,000 trafficked workers), the Xinbi crypto marketplace, three individuals and several London properties.
record.attribution: UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

record.title: Thailand opens seized O'Smach 'scam city' to media and rights groups
record.detail: The Joint Information Centre on the Thai-Cambodian situation led a media inspection of the O'Smach complex, alleging detention rooms, medical facilities and scam workstations, and offered to host international organisations such as Amnesty International.
record.attribution: Thai Joint Information Centre (ACM Prapas Sonjaidee)

record.title: O'Smach Resort compound (Thai-held)
record.detail: AP reported the 80-hectare O'Smach Resort had 157 buildings, 29 used for scam operations, and an estimated 10,000 workers per the Thai military; it is owned by US-sanctioned Cambodian tycoon Ly Yong Phat and was seized by Thai forces in December 2025.

record.title: US sanctions Cambodian senator Kok An and 28 others over scam network
record.detail: OFAC designated Senator Kok An, his Crown Resorts and 28 other persons and entities, saying casinos and resorts in Poipet, Sihanoukville and Bavet were converted into scam compounds; Heng Feng Cambodia Bank was among those designated.

record.title: US offers $10m reward over DKBA-protected Tai Chang scam estate
record.detail: The Irrawaddy reported the US State Department offered up to $10 million for information leading to seizure of Tai Chang scam estate proceeds in Kyauk Khet, and that US prosecutors charged two Chinese nationals over the Shunda Park compound in Min Let Pan.
record.attribution: US State Department / US Justice Department

record.title: Tai Chang scam estate, Kyauk Khet (DKBA area)
record.detail: Named by US authorities as a scam estate in Kyauk Khet operating under DKBA protection; The Irrawaddy later reported operations moving from Kyauk Khet to DKBA headquarters at Sone See Myaing.
record.attribution: US State Department via The Irrawaddy

record.title: Shunda Park, Min Let Pan
record.detail: US prosecutors named Shunda Park in Min Let Pan village, Karen State, as a scam compound; it was reported seized by anti-regime forces in November 2025.
record.attribution: US Justice Department via The Irrawaddy

record.title: Myanmar military raids remote scam compound in Mong Pan
record.detail: Shan Herald reported military authorities arrested 52 Chinese and 4 Myanmar nationals at a remote compound about 20 miles north of Mong Pan town, seizing computers and Starlink units; further arrests were reported in Tachileik (27 Apr) and Muse (29 Apr).

record.title: Scam operations resume in Shwe Kokko in rented houses and hotels
record.detail: The Irrawaddy reported syndicates restarted in Shwe Kokko from late February, dispersing into rented houses, guesthouses and hotels under the Karen National Army (ex-BGF), with Chinese the majority of workers and growing numbers of Pakistani, Indian and Myanmar nationals.

record.title: Thmor Da casino scam base (Thai-held)
record.detail: The Nation reported Thai forces had taken control of the Thmor Da casino area opposite Trat as one of several border scam bases collectively valued at about 10 billion baht.

record.title: Chong An Ma scam base (Thai-held)
record.detail: The Nation listed the Chong An Ma area on the Ubon Ratchathani frontier among scam bases Thai forces said they had captured and would hold 'for as long as it takes'.

record.title: Thailand says it will hold captured border scam bases indefinitely
record.detail: Thai military said it controls scam bases at O'Smach (over 160 buildings in zones A-G), Thmor Da, Chong An Ma and casino areas opposite Sa Kaeo, worth about 10 billion baht, and will keep control to stop networks returning.
record.prov: Surin / Trat / Ubon Ratchathani / Sa Kaeo

record.title: Cambodia deports 635 Thais after Poipet 13-storey building raid
record.detail: Cambodian authorities raided 'Building F', a 13-storey building about 3 km from the border in Poipet, and returned 635 Thais via Ban Khlong Luek checkpoint; Thai screening found 68 complaint case IDs linked to some returnees and about 580 were allowed home.

record.title: Poipet 'Building F' scam and gambling building
record.detail: The Nation described a 13-storey building ('Building F') in Poipet about 3 km from the Thai border raided by Cambodian authorities for suspected scam and online gambling operations.

record.title: Three Poipet returnees arrested on outstanding warrants
record.detail: Sa Kaeo police said warrant checks on the 635 repatriated Thais led to the arrest of three people wanted for offences including murder, embezzlement and illegal online gambling/money laundering.

record.title: 18 Thais returning from Cambodia held over mule-account links
record.detail: Chanthaburi police detained 18 Thais at Ban Phak Kad crossing after they completed Cambodian prison sentences; seven were listed as linked to scam mule accounts in over 60 fraud cases and four had warrants.

record.title: 16 people fleeing Poipet scam compound caught at border
record.detail: Burapha Task Force and ranger units intercepted 16 people crossing via natural routes: 4 Thais (recruited to an online gambling site in Poipet), 2 Vietnamese and 10 Shan migrants from Myanmar.
record.place: Ban Phu Nam Kliang, Pa Rai

record.title: Yong Nee Oo Resort scam hub (UWSA area)
record.detail: A Shan Human Rights Foundation report described Yong Nee Oo Resort as a UWSA-controlled scam hub, with survivors allegedly moved to a rare-earth mine near Mong Sat less than 8 km from the Thai border.

record.title: KK Park (largely demolished)
record.detail: The Irrawaddy cited regime claims that 635 buildings were demolished and 2,000 arrested at KK Park, while only 3 of 77 marked buildings in Shwe Kokko had been razed over five months.
record.attribution: Myanmar regime claims via The Irrawaddy

record.title: Junta resumes demolishing Shwe Kokko and KK Park buildings
record.detail: Thai officials in Mae Sot reported two backhoes demolishing scam-linked buildings in Shwe Kokko and KK Park at about two buildings a day; analysts said earlier demolitions were largely performative.
record.attribution: Thai officials in Mae Sot; GI-TOC analyst

record.title: Junta marks 77 Shwe Kokko buildings for demolition
record.detail: Karen News reported the junta, with BGF/KNA cooperation, inspected over 300 illegal structures, identified 77 buildings running scams and had 74 left to demolish as of 25 May; critics called it symbolic.
record.attribution: Myanmar junta state media; KIC source

record.title: Recruiter who lured Thais to Tbong Khmum compound arrested
record.detail: The police Anti-Trafficking in Persons Division, using data shared by Meta, arrested an alleged ringleader in eastern Thailand accused of luring Thais to a scam compound in Tbong Khmum, Cambodia; at least five victims filed complaints.

record.title: Thailand reports 24bn baht seized in nine-month scam crackdown
record.detail: The Nation reported authorities seized over 24 billion baht in assets, closed 351,884 mule accounts and arrested 29,233 suspects, listing dismantled border scam bases including O'Smach, Thmor Da, Poipet, KK Park, Shwe Kokko, Minletpan, Tachileik and Bokeo.

record.title: OFAC expands Prince Group sanctions, hits Thailand-based hotel firm
record.detail: Treasury designated 9 individuals and 26 entities tied to the Cambodia-based Prince Group TCO, including Thailand-based White Horse Hotel Management Group Co., Ltd.

record.title: Rights group says 5,300+ still held in DKBA-area scam centres
record.detail: Thai-based CSNHTV told Thai police more than 5,300 people, including about 1,600 Chinese and 200 Myanmar nationals, remain in four locations in DKBA-controlled areas near the Thai border.
record.attribution: Civil Society Network for Human Trafficking Victim Assistance (CSNHTV)

record.title: Laos deports 24 Thais suspected of scam work via Chiang Khong bridge
record.detail: 24 Thai nationals (15 men, 9 women) suspected of working for call-centre scam networks were handed over at the 4th Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge; two had outstanding warrants and Thai cyber police opened an investigation.

record.title: 11 people fleeing Poipet jobs arrested crossing into Sa Kaeo
record.detail: Burapha Task Force soldiers arrested 7 Bangladeshis, 2 Vietnamese, 1 Chinese and 1 Thai who said they fled unpaid work in Poipet and paid smugglers 8,000 baht each to cross.
record.place: Ban Ang Sila, Non Mak Mun

record.title: Junta claims 69 Shwe Kokko scam buildings demolished
record.detail: The junta said it demolished 69 scam buildings in Shwe Kokko; residents quoted by Mon News called it political theatre and said operations continue at Shwe Kokko, Phalu, Kyaukhtat and near Ma Htaw Thalay.
record.attribution: Myanmar junta; residents via Mon News

record.title: 'AA' complex near Ma Htaw Thalay
record.detail: BNI/Mon News residents named a complex called 'AA' near Ma Htaw Thalay as still active in Myawaddy Township.

record.title: Phalu scam sites (DKBA security)
record.detail: Residents said scam operations remain active at Phalu border gate, where the DKBA provides security.

record.title: Laos raids Vientiane scam base, 589 held including 373 Thais
record.detail: Lao Ministry of Public Security's special anti-scam unit raided a building in Ban Dong Phosi, Hadxaifong, detaining 589 people: 373 Thai, 199 Lao, 15 Vietnamese and 2 Cambodian.

record.title: EU sanctions DKBA, Prince Group and Jin Bei Group over scam centres
record.detail: The Council of the EU listed seven persons and three entities, including the DKBA (Karen State near Myawaddy), Prince Holding Group and chairman Chen Zhi, and Jin Bei Group and chairman Zhu Zhongbiao, with asset freezes and travel bans.

record.title: Cambodia claims scam compounds eradicated; experts sceptical
record.detail: Cambodia's anti-scam commission said 624 of 793 suspected sites were raided, about 30,000 detained and 58,266 foreigners deported; Amnesty International and an anti-trafficking consultant were sceptical. Al Jazeera named O'Smach Casino at the Chong Chom crossing.

record.title: Myanmar Witness says Shwe Kokko demolition claims were faked
record.detail: Myanmar Witness analysis of the regime's claimed 25 May-26 July demolition of 77 of 322 structures found mislocated sites, AI-generated imagery and exaggerated building heights.

record.title: OFAC sanctions Xinbi Guarantee marketplace
record.detail: Treasury designated Xinbi Guarantee, Singapore-based SafeW Technology and Cambodia-based Anwen Technology, saying the marketplace processed over $24 billion mainly in Southeast Asia.

record.title: Sone See Myaing (DKBA HQ) scam relocation
record.detail: The Irrawaddy reported Chinese-run scam operations relocating from Kyauk Khet to the DKBA headquarters at Sone See Myaing, citing residents and Telegram job ads.

record.title: Shwe Kokko: at least 18 new scam sites
record.detail: The Irrawaddy said at least 18 new sites were identified in Shwe Kokko by early September, and listed active operations at Thitkate village, Hpakalu, Payathonzu, Sone See Myaing, Hpalu and Myawaddy.

record.title: Payathonzu (Three Pagodas Pass) scam activity
record.detail: The Irrawaddy listed Hpaya Thonezu (Payathonzu), opposite Sangkhla Buri, among Karen State locations with active scam operations.

record.title: Minivan plunges into ravine on Highway 304
record.detail: Khaosod English reports a passenger minivan left the road at km 243 and rolled into a ravine; police attributed it to driver fatigue.

record.title: New Year 'seven dangerous days' road toll: 272 dead
record.detail: DDPM reported 1,511 crashes, 272 deaths and 1,464 injuries over the 30 Dec 2025–5 Jan 2026 holiday campaign; Bangkok had the most deaths (22), per The Nation.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: Tour speedboat sinks after collision with trawler off Koh Khiao
record.detail: A tour speedboat carrying about 55 people collided with a fishing trawler between Phuket and Koh Phi Phi and sank; one foreign tourist died and 22 were injured, per Thai Examiner. The operator was detained.
record.agency: Maritime Security Command Region 3; Marine Department

record.title: Construction crane falls on express train at Sikhio
record.detail: A launching gantry for the Bangkok–Nong Khai high-speed rail project collapsed onto express train No. 21 (Bangkok–Ubon Ratchathani) near km 220, derailing it. Wikipedia lists 30 dead and 69 injured; Northeastern Line services resumed normally on 24 January.
record.place: Ban Thanon Khot, railway km 220 between Nong Nam Khun and Sikhio stations
record.agency: State Railway of Thailand; Department of Rail Transport

record.title: Crane and girder collapse on Rama II elevated motorway works
record.detail: A launching gantry and concrete segment fell from the M82 elevated motorway project near the Tha Chin River bridge, crushing two vehicles; The Nation reported 2 dead and 5 injured, with heavy congestion both ways.
record.place: Rama II Road near Tha Chin River bridge ascent, Tha Chin subdistrict

record.title: Sinkhole swallows pickup on inbound Rama II Road
record.detail: The inbound road surface collapsed near the Big Song shopping centre, and a pickup fell in; officials suspected a burst water main. The section was closed, causing heavy congestion both ways, according to The Nation.
record.place: Rama II Road inbound near Big Song shopping centre

record.title: Highways Dept closes Rama II main road for 60 days after crane collapse
record.detail: The Department of Highways said it would close the affected Rama II main road section in the M82 project area for 60 days and reviewed ending the contract, according to The Nation.
record.place: Rama II Road, Bang Khun Thian–Ban Phaeo motorway project section

record.title: Check-in system fault causes long queues at Suvarnabhumi
record.detail: Thaiger reports Thai Airways' self-service kiosks could not print bag tags after a new baggage policy took effect, pushing passengers to staffed counters and creating long queues.

record.title: Hauliers threaten nationwide stoppage over diesel crisis, cite Laem Chabang delays
record.detail: The Land Transport Federation of Thailand demanded a diesel price cap and cutting truck turnaround at Laem Chabang Port to 3–4 hours per trip. It warned of a nationwide transport suspension if ignored, per The Nation.

record.title: Songkran 'seven dangerous days' road toll: 242 dead
record.detail: DDPM reported 1,242 crashes, 242 deaths and 1,200 injuries over 10–16 April; Bangkok had the most deaths (21), and speeding and motorcycles dominated, per The Nation.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: Nine killed as pickup overturns on steep Nan mountain road
record.detail: A family pickup lost control on a downhill bend at km 8+700 of the Pua–Bo Kluea road and overturned, killing nine (including children) and injuring 14, per The Nation.

record.title: Thai–Cambodian land border stays shut into 10th month
record.detail: The Nation reported that land crossings with Cambodia had been closed since 23 June 2025. Officials said they were unlikely to reopen in 2026, which hit cross-border traffic and trade.
record.place: Thai–Cambodian land border (Chanthaburi, Trat, Surin, Ubon Ratchathani crossings)

record.title: Pratunam flyover shut ~10 months for Orange Line works
record.detail: MRTA closed the Pratunam flyover on Phetchaburi Road from 24 April 2026 to 11 February 2027 for underground Orange Line works and published five detour routes, per The Nation.
record.agency: Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand

record.title: Border gate stays shut at Khlong Luek, stranding repatriation of 635 Thais
record.detail: Khaosod English reports that Cambodian officials at Poipet kept the gate at the Friendship Bridge crossing closed without explanation, delaying the handover of 635 Thai nationals.
record.place: Khlong Luek checkpoint, Thai–Cambodian Friendship Bridge

record.title: Tour bus crash on rain-slick Highway 304 injures 35
record.detail: A tour bus collided with a truck and a pickup on a steep, curving section and left the road; The Nation reported 35 injured, one critically, and no deaths.

record.title: Freight train hits city bus at Makkasan crossing; bus burns
record.detail: A freight train from Chachoengsao struck a BMTA route 23 bus at the crossing near Airport Rail Link Makkasan station and dragged it about 50 m; the bus caught fire. Khaosod English reported 8 killed and more than 20 injured.
record.place: Level crossing near Makkasan station, Asok–Din Daeng Road
record.agency: State Railway of Thailand; BMTA; DDPM

record.title: Boulders block Highway 108 in Mae Hong Son, vehicles stranded
record.detail: A landslide dropped boulders across both directions at km 301 (Mae Surin section); they were too large for local equipment, and many vehicles were stranded, per Thaiger.

record.title: Four killed in pickup–sedan collision in Wiang Chai
record.detail: A pickup and a sedan collided at the Ban Ling Kunchon traffic-light junction; four died and one was critically injured, per Chiang Rai Times.
record.place: Ban Ling Kunchon intersection, Don Sila

record.title: Factory shuttle bus rams school transport, 24 students hurt
record.detail: On the first day of term a factory shuttle bus hit the rear of a school transport vehicle on Road 3079; 24 students were injured, five moderately, per Khaosod English.
record.place: Road 3079 near housing estate, Tha Tum subdistrict

record.title: Hat Yai runway closed after fire-engine accident
record.detail: Hat Yai International Airport closed Runway 26 from 13:55 to 16:30 after an airport fire engine accident; two inbound flights diverted to Krabi, per The Nation.

record.title: Double-decker coach hits parked lorry on Highway 201, 15 hurt
record.detail: An overnight coach from Bangkok's Mo Chit terminal crashed into an 18-wheel lorry parked on the roadside, injuring 15, per Khaosod English.

record.title: Construction barge capsizes off Samut Prakan pier
record.detail: Khaosod English reports that a construction barge overturned near a private pier opposite Suk Sawat Soi 84, leaving two people in the water; the cause was under investigation.
record.place: Chao Phraya River opposite Suk Sawat Soi 84

record.title: Roads closed after water floods Purple Line tunnel shaft
record.detail: MRTA closed all lanes of Prajadhipok Road between Ban Khaek and Wongwian Yai after groundwater entered a South Purple Line construction shaft, per Khaosod English.
record.agency: Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand

record.title: Chiang Rai city road closed for flood-damage repairs
record.detail: Highway 1232 from King Mengrai Monument to the Nong Bua junction was closed from 10 July to 20 September to rebuild a storm-weakened road base, per Chiang Rai Times.
record.place: Highway 1232, King Mengrai Monument–Nong Bua junction
record.agency: Department of Highways (Chiang Rai Highway District 1)

record.title: Thai AirAsia pulls nine domestic routes from Suvarnabhumi
record.detail: Thai AirAsia suspended nine domestic routes from Suvarnabhumi from 15 July to 30 September, moving them to Don Mueang. The Nation said high fuel costs and weak demand were the reasons.

record.title: School bus overturns in Surin, 57 hurt
record.detail: A school bus from Khukhan (Sisaket) lost control and overturned in front of Wat Taluak; 51 students and 6 teachers had minor injuries, per Khaosod English.
record.place: Highway 214 in front of Wat Taluak, Kang Aen subdistrict

record.title: Airport Rail Link car derails at Khlong Tan depot
record.detail: A car derailed at switch 3018 while entering the depot at 00:47, leaving one train in service that morning. SRT added trains and shuttle buses between Makkasan and Suvarnabhumi, per The Nation.
record.agency: State Railway of Thailand; Department of Rail Transport

record.title: Airport Rail Link runs single-track at 30-minute intervals
record.detail: Technical issues forced single-track running with a train every 30 minutes, adding about 30 minutes from Phaya Thai to Suvarnabhumi. Free shuttle buses ran between Makkasan and the airport, per The Nation.

record.title: Longtail tour boat capsizes in big swell off Ao Nang
record.detail: A wave capsized a longtail carrying 10 tourists near Laem Hang Nak; all 12 aboard were rescued, with 6 minor injuries, per Thai Examiner.
record.place: Near Laem Hang Nak, between Ao Nang and Hong Island
record.agency: Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park

record.title: Flash floods in Nan collapse bridge on Pua–Bo Kluea route
record.detail: Over 200mm of rain caused floods in several Nan districts; a bridge on Highway 1256 (Pua–Bo Kluea) collapsed and the Phayaeng–Kiew Muang road became impassable, per Khaosod English.

record.title: Nan floods close roads and a city bridge
record.detail: The Nation reported that Route 1256 was closed after power poles fell, Woranakhon Road in Tha Wang Pha was impassable and Nakhon Nan Pattana Bridge was scheduled to close. The same report put the flood toll at two dead.
record.place: Tha Wang Pha market and Nan town

record.title: Thousands of flight delays at Bangkok airports over three days
record.detail: AirHelp reported 2,316 delays and 143 cancellations at Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang on 21–23 August. It attributed them to heavy traffic, tight ground-handling buffers and thunderstorms.

record.title: Landslide blocks Nan–Phayao Highway 1148
record.detail: Overnight rain brought mud and large trees across both lanes at km 73+250 (Sakoen–Sop Thu); heavy machinery was sent and detours set up, per The Nation.

record.title: Flooding shuts Highway 401 toward Phuket, tourists evacuated
record.detail: Floodwater made Highway 401 at km 66+600 impassable for small vehicles; DDPM evacuated stranded tourists in high-clearance trucks, and traffic was sent via Highway 4118, per Khaosod English.

record.title: Landslide blocks a lane of Highway 12 in Phetchabun
record.detail: Soil and rocks blocked one lane at km 373+400, per The Nation.

record.title: Landslide severs road in Phanom, Surat Thani
record.detail: A landslide cut the road between Ban Saphan Tao and Ban Khlong Phum Duang, leaving it impassable, per The Nation.
record.place: Ban Saphan Tao–Ban Khlong Phum Duang, Khlong Sok subdistrict

record.title: Landslide and flash flood hit Rural Road MS 3007, Khun Yuam
record.detail: Soil slid onto Rural Road MS 3007 between Ban Mae Sape Tai and Ban Mae Sape Nuea, per The Nation.
record.place: Rural Road MS 3007, Ban Mae Sape Tai–Ban Mae Sape Nuea

record.title: Flash floods damage bridge approaches in Wiang Haeng
record.detail: Landslides and flash floods damaged two bridge approaches and blocked village roads in Wiang Haeng district, per The Nation.

record.title: Track cable fire halts MRT Blue and Purple lines
record.detail: An electrical short in a power cable caused a fire between Tao Poon and Bang Pho around 12:30. BEM suspended services and ran shuttle buses, and normal service resumed on the morning of 21 September, per Thai PBS World. No injuries were reported.

record.title: Torrential rain floods Pattaya roads up to 1 m
record.detail: Water nearly 1 m deep made Pattaya Third Road, Sukhumvit near the Pattaya intersection and Railway Road impassable for small vehicles; dangerous sections were closed, per Pattaya Mail.
record.place: Pattaya Third Road, Sukhumvit Road, Railway Road

record.title: Highway 331 submerged in Si Racha, Pattaya streets flooded
record.detail: The Nation reported all lanes of Highway 331 flooded from the Pinthong 1 flyover to the Nong Kham interchange. Many Pattaya roads also flooded, stalling cars and motorcycles.

record.title: Heavy rain floods major roads across Bangkok and suburbs
record.detail: After up to 105.5mm of rain, roads including Vibhavadi Rangsit, Ngam Wong Wan, Chaeng Watthana, Ram Inthra and Phahonyothin flooded, causing standstill traffic, per The Nation.
record.place: Vibhavadi Rangsit Rd (Lak Si) and other roads

record.title: Two cold waves forecast after New Year
record.detail: Thaiger, citing TMD forecasts, said two cool spells would hit upper Thailand on Jan 4-11 and Jan 14-15, with Bangkok's coldest morning around 18.4°C expected on Jan 9.

record.title: Cold air deepens over upper Thailand; lower South stormy
record.detail: TMD said a cold air mass from China would drop temperatures 2-4°C in upper Thailand while heavy rain hit Nakhon Si Thammarat, Phatthalung, Songkhla, Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat; Gulf waves 2-3 m.

record.title: Frost at Doi Inthanon and Phu Luang
record.detail: The Nation reported the season's first frost: 0°C at Doi Inthanon's Kew Mae Pan (grass -1.2°C) and 4°C at Phu Luang in Loei.
record.place: Doi Inthanon summit / Kew Mae Pan

record.title: New cold surge forecast Jan 21-25
record.detail: TMD forecast a moderate high-pressure system from China to cut temperatures 2-4°C on Jan 21-25; northern lows 11-18°C with mountain tops 3-12°C.

record.title: Cooler weather returns Feb 1
record.detail: TMD said a new moderate high-pressure area from China would bring cooler conditions from Feb 1 after a warm, hazy spell on Jan 26-31.

record.title: Government orders all provinces to prepare for 2026 drought
record.detail: The NDPMC told all provinces to set up water monitoring, contingency plans and water trucks/pumps for the dry season, citing possible El Niño from as early as March.
record.agency: National Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Command

record.title: Storms damage hundreds of homes in Chiang Mai
record.detail: Storms on Feb 20-21 hit Chom Thong, Doi Lo, Phrao and Mae Wang districts, affecting at least 490 households; hail of 1-2 cm and minor injuries from broken glass were reported.
record.place: Chom Thong and Doi Lo districts

record.title: TMD declares start of 2026 summer
record.detail: TMD said summer began on Feb 22 and would last to mid-May, with highs of 42-43°C possible in Mae Hong Son, Lampang and Tak from mid-March to April.

record.title: TMD advisory No.1 on summer storms for Mar 3-6
record.detail: TMD warned of thunderstorms, gusty winds, hail and lightning across upper Thailand including Bangkok on Mar 3-6.

record.title: Government warns heat index may exceed 52°C
record.detail: The PM's Office warned the 2026 heat index could exceed 52°C, with North, Northeast and Central regions most at risk in April-May.

record.title: Heat index could reach 60°C in early April
record.detail: The Digital Economy and Society Ministry, citing TMD, confirmed that the heat index could rise to 60°C in early April.
record.agency: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society

record.title: Extreme heat forecast before Songkran
record.detail: Citing TMD data, The Nation reported highs of 40-43°C in the North and upper Central region and 35-41°C in Bangkok on Apr 8-9.

record.title: Summer squall damages homes in Chaiyaphum
record.detail: An early-morning storm tore roofs off homes, uprooted trees and crushed vehicles around Ban Khai market in Mueang district.

record.title: Fist-sized hail pummels Phu Kradueng village
record.detail: Hail some reported as egg- or fist-sized punched holes in zinc roofs of 4-5 houses and toppled power poles in Huai Som subdistrict; no deaths reported.

record.title: Hailstorms hit northern Chiang Mai and Khao Kho
record.detail: Hail and storms damaged roofs and crops in Chai Prakan, Fang, Chiang Dao and Mae Ai districts of Chiang Mai and the Khao Kho area of Phetchabun; no injuries reported.

record.title: Bangkok heat index in dangerous range
record.detail: Bangkok's forecast heat index reached 42-51.9°C ('danger' level), with authorities saying heat had overtaken air pollution as the main health concern.
record.agency: Bangkok Air Quality Information Centre / TMD

record.title: Summer storm tears through Korat
record.detail: Strong winds and rain on the evening of Apr 24 damaged domes, homes and trees in Mueang, Phimai and Non Sung districts; no casualties reported.

record.title: Storms topple power poles, one dead
record.detail: Evening storms toppled about 140 power poles in Chai Nat, Nakhon Pathom and Suphan Buri; an elderly woman died in Chai Nat and at least 3 were injured in Nakhon Pathom.
record.place: Chai Nat, Nakhon Pathom, Suphan Buri

record.title: Windstorms damage 141 houses in three provinces
record.detail: The AHA Centre, citing provincial DDPM offices, reported 141 houses damaged in Tak (77), Nakhon Sawan (51) and Sukhothai (13); no casualties.

record.title: El Niño risk flags raw-water shortages
record.detail: TMD forecast El Niño from May-July; PWA said 20 branches in 17 provinces faced raw-water shortages, per The Nation.
record.attribution: The Nation, citing TMD and PWA

record.title: TMD declares start of 2026 rainy season
record.detail: TMD said the rainy season began May 15, with rainfall ~10% below normal, a dry spell late June-early July and 1-2 tropical storms likely in Aug-Sep.

record.title: Six Andaman provinces warned of floods
record.detail: DDPM warned Ranong, Phang Nga, Phuket, Krabi, Trang and Satun of flash floods and landslides on Jun 3-8 from a strong southwest monsoon; waves up to 3 m.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: TMD warns 63 provinces of heavy rain
record.detail: TMD said a monsoon trough plus a South China Sea low would bring thunderstorms to 63 provinces, with 80% coverage on the western South coast.

record.title: Chiang Khong warned of flash floods
record.detail: DDPM, citing TMD, warned Chiang Khong district of flash floods and landslides on Jun 30-Jul 3 from a monsoon trough.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: Tropical Storm Maysak boosts monsoon rain
record.detail: TMD said Maysak (~65 km/h) would cross Hainan into southern China Jul 4-6 without hitting Thailand, but put 15 provinces on heavy-rain red alert Jul 3-6.

record.title: Heavy rain warning Jul 26-30; Typhoon Noul bypasses Thailand
record.detail: TMD warned of heavy to very heavy rain and flash floods Jul 26-30 from a strengthening monsoon; Typhoon Noul was forecast to hit Guangdong, not Thailand.

record.title: 15 provinces warned of landslides
record.detail: The Department of Mineral Resources warned 15 provinces of landslides Jul 30-Aug 1 after some areas logged over 150 mm of rain in 24 hours.

record.title: Lightning kills footballer during match
record.detail: Lightning struck a regional tournament match at a stadium in Sungai Golok during heavy rain, killing a player and injuring 12, police said.

record.title: Mekong forecast to rise 1-1.5 m
record.detail: HII/ONWR/DDPM warned the Mekong would rise 1.0-1.5 m on Aug 8-12 along seven riverside provinces from Chiang Rai to Ubon Ratchathani.

record.title: Record rainfall floods Nan
record.detail: Torrential rain from Aug 18 flooded Pua, Tha Wang Pha, Mueang and other districts; Bo Kluea logged 388 mm in 4 hours, two people died and about 8,000 households were affected in Pua.

record.title: 21 provinces warned as depression nears Hainan
record.detail: TMD warned 21 provinces of heavy rain Aug 22-23; a depression over Hainan was set to become a tropical storm but not enter Thailand.

record.title: TMD tracks four Pacific storms, none toward Thailand
record.detail: TMD monitored Tropical Storms Narra and Gaenari, Typhoon Saudel and Depression Atsani; none were expected to enter Thailand, though Narra could add rain in the North and Northeast.

record.title: DDPM warns 51 provinces of floods
record.detail: DDPM warned 51 provinces of flash floods Aug 29-Sep 2, with high risk in Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Tak, Bueng Kan, Nakhon Phanom, Sakon Nakhon, Chanthaburi and Trat.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: 54 provinces warned of flash floods and landslides
record.detail: DDPM warned 54 provinces including Bangkok for Sep 4-7 as a monsoon trough brought heavy rain; threshold cited as over 90 mm in 24 hours.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: TMD warning No.6: heavy rain through Sep 13
record.detail: TMD warned of heavy to very heavy rain to Sep 13 as the monsoon trough shifted south, and said a South China Sea low could become a tropical cyclone heading for northern Vietnam.

record.title: Vietnam low brings very heavy rain risk to Ubon and Trat
record.detail: TMD said a strong low over Vietnam had low odds of becoming a storm but could strengthen the monsoon, with isolated very heavy rain in Ubon Ratchathani and Trat on Sep 14-15.

record.title: All provinces on five-day flood alert
record.detail: DDPM put all provinces on flood alert Sep 16-20 as a cold air mass and stronger monsoon drove the monsoon trough across Thailand; Andaman waves 2-3 m.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: Bangkok and 70 provinces warned of flash floods
record.detail: DDPM warned Bangkok and 70 provinces of flash floods, landslides and rough seas Sep 23-27 as a strong low approached from central Vietnam.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation

record.title: 43 provinces on high alert through Sep 27
record.detail: TMD's warning cited a strong low over Cambodia and an active monsoon trough, bringing heavy rain to 43 provinces and 2-3 m waves.

record.title: Prolonged rain floods Bangkok roads
record.detail: BMA reported 105.5 mm in 24 hours in Khlong Sam Wa and 92.5 mm in Sai Mai, flooding Vibhavadi Rangsit, Chaeng Watthana and other roads.

record.title: TMD: heavy rain across most of Thailand to Sep 27
record.detail: TMD said a strong low crossing the Central region would bring heavy to very heavy rain over 80% of Bangkok and vicinity Sep 25-27, with 3 m+ waves in thunderstorms.

record.title: Khao Yai National Park closed by flash floods
record.detail: Khao Yai closed Sep 26-27 after persistent heavy rain caused flash flooding, impassable roads and mudslide risk, the park said.

record.title: 'Kami menghampirinya kerana sangka dia mahu serah diri' - Anggota Polis cedera dilibas parang
record.detail: Rantau Panjang: Seorang anggota polis berpangkat koperal tidak menyangka operasi rutin membanteras dadah nyaris meragut nyawanya apabila suspek dikejar melibas tangan kirinya menggunakan parang.

record.detail_en: At about 11:49 p.m. on October 15, 2011, the Seventh Patrol District Command of the Marine Commission received a call from people calling the special reporting line "118" to say that foreign visitors were suspected of illegally touching sea turtles at Hanabi-Iwa Beach, which is a famous tourist destination in Ko Ryukyu Island. The investigation record was completed according to law and after requesting prosecutors from Taiwan's Pindong Local Prosecutor's Office to show them the video footage, last night they coordinated the cross-border arrest of the boat and sent it back to Taiwan for investigation by the Pindong Provincial Investigation Department.

record.title_en: In response to the suspected death of a Russian person from plague, WHO has investigated through the International Health Regulations mechanism and continued monitoring both domestically and internationally.
record.detail_en: The Russian Federation's Department of Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said on October 6, 2026 that in response to recent international media reports that the Irkutsk region of Siberia reported a case of pneumonia death from unknown cause today (October 2, 2126), the patient was a 28-year-old female laboratory technician at the Irkutsky Institute for Epidemiology. She died after developing severe pneumonia on October 2, according to local Russian media quoted an official statement issued by the official agency for control of infectious diseases (Rospotrebnadzor). According to the results of extensive tests performed by the infected employee, no special microorganism related to her work was found; the country's expert committee on biosecurity also confirmed that there was no accidental release of pathogen from the laboratory. In addition, Russia has carried out extensive testing and hospital isolation observation of all contacts, and currently only two cases of COVID-19 have been detected.

record.title_en: Chinese police vessels 3301 and 3323 violated Dongsha restricted waters.
record.detail_en: At 14:00 today (16), the Dongsha Command Department of the Coast Guard detected two coast guard vessels such as "China Coast Guard 3301" and "China Coast Guard 3303" in the southwest of the Dongsha Sea. According to the direction and speed of the two vessels, they may sail into the waters restricted by me. The Dongsha Command Department immediately reported the online service ships "Flagship" and "PP-10032" to the deployment site. At 1534, the "China Coast Guard 3301" and "China Coast Guard 3303" sailed into the restricted waters. The "Flagship" and "PP-10032" patrol boats immediately adopted a "one-to-one" approach for simultaneous monitoring, and were strongly dispersed in Chinese and English broadcasts. The confrontation is still ongoing at the scene. The Coast Guard said that since this (115) year, the Coast Guard has deported 11 and 14 Chinese Coast Guard vessels from Dongsha waters. The Coast Guard emphasizes that China has indisputable sovereignty over Dongsha Atoll and its surrounding waters.

record.detail_en: The command department of the Coast Guard's Fifth Patrol District received a notification from the Mai Liu Harbor Signal Station at 18:00 yesterday (15). The coast guard personnel carried out an injury assessment immediately, giving care and warmth. record.detail: The Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is in a phase of intense transmission.
